title: Private deployment state orchestrator and safe Terraform fallback runbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create an operational runbook and an automated remediation orchestrator for common Private (VPC) health-check failures. The artifact should specify a state-machine for detection -> safe remediation -> verification -> rollback, concrete Terraform fallback actions (taint/replace with drift guards), and the human-in-loop escalation criteria. Focus on reliability, minimizing blast radius, and auditability for regulated customers.
runbook_steps: 1) Detect: Validate alert source and scope. Confirm alert originates from Synthetic VPC probe (control-plane heartbeat), node health (worker heartbeats), or network path checks (subnet ACL / NACL drift). Query the console trace, last 30m heartbeats, and node metrics to determine whether failure is localized or systemic.

2) Triage: Add initial incident note in the console incident timeline and Slack channel #private-incidents. Tag customer(s) if request originates from a dedicated tenant. Record metric deltas: CPU, GPU memory, socket errors, connection resets, and LB 5xx rate.

3) Quick containment: If failure is isolated to a single node and customer impact is low, mark node as DRAINING via the control plane and reroute traffic to healthy nodes. Emit an audit event with request id and operator id or automated-controller id.

4) Automated remediation attempt (safe path): Evaluate if safe automated actions are allowed per policy (see Safety Controls). If allowed, run the state-machine: cordon -> capture logs + kernel traces -> attempt soft-restart of the node agent -> if soft-restart fails, perform Terraform plan with a targeted taint of the failed resource and apply with replace_count=1 and strict drift check. Limit replacement concurrency to 1 per AZ per minute.

5) Verification: After remediation, run a focused synthetic probe sequence (control-plane heartbeat, inference light request, KV cache warmup). Verify metrics return to within 10% of baseline for 5 consecutive minutes before marking the node healthy. Post a verification block in the incident timeline with timestamps and snapshot links.

6) Escalation: If automated remediation fails twice or customer_impact==high, escalate to on-call SRE and enable manual approval for further Terraform changes. Capture video/screenshots of console flows and attach PRs to the incident doc.

7) Rollback and recovery: If a remediation degrades other systems or raises error budget risk, trigger a controlled rollback using the recorded backup plan (terraform apply with previous statefile or rollback module) and run canary traffic to validate.

8) Postmortem actions: Create a follow-up ticket with root-cause hypothesis, instrumentation gaps, and a quantifiable run-rate for the automated action. If remediation used taint/replace frequently, schedule long-term fix (kernel patch, config change) and update the terraform module to prevent recurring drift.

9) Audit and compliance: Store all terraform applies, plan outputs, and operator approvals in the secure audit bucket with KMS encryption and retention policy. Publish a redacted incident timeline to the customer-facing compliance folder when required.
10) Continuous improvement: Add failing probe patterns to the optimize engine for future batching/eviction heuristics and create alerts that map to the runbook sections to reduce MTTR over time.
automation_behaviour: State machine model: states = {observed, triaged, soft_remediate, taint_replace, verify, escalated, rollback, resolved}. Transitions are triggered by probe results and timeouts. Each transition is idempotent and records a monotonic operation id.

Controller safeguards: every automated Terraform apply must run a dry-run (plan) and be approved by a policy engine that enforces: change_scope <= resource_count_threshold, no global network changes, and max_replacements_per_run <= 1.
Backoff strategy: exponential backoff with jitter between remediation attempts (initial 30s, factor 2, max 10m). After 2 automated failures switch to manual-only mode for that workload.
Rate limiting: global and per-customer rate limits for automated replaces (default 2 replacements per 10 minutes per account) to avoid cascading capacity storms.

Observability hooks: every state transition emits a structured event to the console (auditId, state, reason, operator), and emits metrics for success/failure/latency to the console dashboard for SLIs.

Safe-taint pattern: apply targeted taint to cloud instance or terraform resource representing the unhealthy node. Taint is accompanied by a tag 'auto-remediate:<id>' and a TTL metadata so other operators can filter automated actions.

Canary window: when performing replacements that touch multiple instances in an AZ, perform a single replacement first (canary) and verify for 5m before allowing roll-forward for additional replacements.
Human-in-loop: high-impact changes require manual approval recorded in the audit log; approvals can be granted via console UI or signed GitHub PR merge (GPG/SSO enforced).
safety_controls: Approval policies: 'high blast' changes require two approvers from SRE and Infra Security. Policy enforced by policy engine service (OPA).
Taint TTL and ownership: automated taints expire after 24h unless re-claimed by an operator; expired taints are auto-cleared to avoid permanent drift tags.

Dry-run requirement: every terraform apply must include a plan that is archived and linked in the incident. The controller rejects applies that include network or IAM changes unless explicitly allowed.
Replacement caps: maximum of 2 simultaneous replacements per availability zone and 1 per instance-group to prevent capacity collapse.
Safe-mode flag: can be flipped in the console to pause automated remediation globally or per-customer (used during large outages or regulatory reviews).
Audit and revert scripts: one-click revert in the console that runs pre-recorded rollback steps and creates a GitHub PR for human review if needed.
metrics: SLI: control-plane heartbeat success rate >= 99.95% (5m rolling).
SLO: mean time to remediation (automated) < 3m for isolated node failures.
Alert thresholds: synthetic probe failure count >= 3 within 2 minutes triggers triage.
Remediation success rate: automated taint+replace success >= 95% over a 30d window.
Safety metric: number of automated replacements with manual rollback <= 1 per 90d per cluster.
